cases.final_diagnosis: An intermittent vibration fault on CNC-07 during specific job windows is the likely cause of the inspection failures for jobs 14, 19, and 20.

CNC-01 experienced a real but transient vibration excursion during roughly ticks 520-524: the alarm logged 7.01-7.37 mm/s at ticks 521-524 (E7), and the 520-529 bucket shows max 7.374 mm/s and mean 4.245 mm/s (E4), above the 4.5 mm/s monitoring setpoint. No physical correlate supports a machine fault: CNC-01 load was stable (E6/E9, mean ~66%), power was stable around 11.7 kW (E12), and factory air temperature was normal at 77-78 °F (E13). CNC-02 showed normal vibration in the same window, max 2.144 mm/s (E8), ruling out a factory-wide cause. Vibration returned to 2.28 mm/s by tick 530 and remained below 2.37 mm/s through tick 540 with no recurrence (E4/E11), arguing against a developing fault or a persistent sensor fault. This is a transient alarm/setpoint exceedance, not a confirmed failure, so no intervention is indicated; continue routine monitoring and watch for recurrence on the next job.

The CNC-03 vibration alarm at tick 381 (6.78 mm/s above the 4.50 mm/s threshold) was a one-off transient disturbance on CNC-03, not a persistent fault. CNC-03 vibration peaked at about 6.84 mm/s during roughly ticks 375-384 (E4, E14), then fell to at most 2.15 mm/s during ticks 385-394 and stayed at or below 0.27 mm/s from ticks 395-400 (E12, E14), with no recurrence above 4.5 mm/s after tick 390. Peer machines CNC-01, CNC-02, CNC-04, and CNC-06 all ran with normal vibration (maxima 1.94-2.54 mm/s; E8, E9, E10, E13), and factory air temperature was steady at 75.4-76.4°F during 375-390 (E7), ruling out a peer-transmitted or ambient cause. CNC-03 is running normally now.

CNC-03 raised repeated vibration alarms during ticks 71-78 (up to 5.21 mm/s against the 4.50 mm/s threshold) while the machine was idle and processing no part (every alarm event has job_id null). The vibration has since cleared: 0.375 mm/s at tick 79 and 0.175 mm/s at tick 80, far below the threshold, after being low before the window (ticks 60-69 mean 0.11 mm/s). During the alarm window CNC-03's temperature (68.0-71.9°F, mean 70.0°F), power (1.64-2.35 kW, mean 2.00 kW), and following_error (mean 0.83 µm, max 1.80 µm) were all normal and comparable to the idle baseline CNC-04 (following_error mean 1.18 µm, max 2.29 µm). No genuine mechanical fault is supported: the vibration did not persist while idle, power did not rise with the vibration, and following_error matches the idle baseline. This points to a spurious vibration sensor/signal-path reading on CNC-03 (H1), or at most a cleared transient trip (H3); either way there is no confirmed production fault and no parts were affected.

CNC-04 has a progressive feed-axis servo drive fault: following_error has risen gradually from a ~1.0 µm mean early in the run to a ~17.6 µm mean (max 20.263 µm) in the latest window, tripping the 20.00 µm alarm at tick 1129 while CNC-04 remains running. CNC-01, CNC-02 and CNC-05 following_error stay flat (recent maximum ≈ 6.3–6.7 µm), so this is not line-wide; CNC-03 following_error was not readable in the evidence provided. CNC-04 power is elevated (recent mean ≈ 10.6 vs early ~2.0 baseline), consistent with servo drive strain, and CNC-04 temperature is now about the same as the CNC-01 peer (~112 vs ~111), which argues against a spindle bearing fault (expected to run hotter than peers). Best-supported hypothesis: H_worn_drive_CNC04.

cases.final_diagnosis: CNC-02 feed-axis servo drive wear (progressive axis fault). CNC-02 following_error has risen steadily while running, from a bucket mean of 0.977 µm (ticks 0–59) to 18.555 µm (ticks 1320–1360), peaking at 20.103 µm and tripping the 20.00 µm alarm at tick 1358 (E1, E4). The fault is local to CNC-02: peer machines CNC-01 (E5) and CNC-03 (E13) keep following_error around 3–4 µm across the same window, so it is not line-wide and not an instrument fault (H2 is contradicted by the steady upward trend; H3 is contradicted because the rise is continuous, not a flat step). CNC-02 power is moderately elevated (E6), but vibration is only marginally above CNC-01 (E10 ≈2.4 vs E12 ≈2.0 mm/s) and temperature is only slightly above CNC-01 (E16 ≈117.0 vs E14 ≈109.2 °F), which argues against a binding axis (H4). Inspection failures at jobs 7 and 11 (E9) line up with high following_error, consistent with a real accuracy defect rather than a passing-part fluke. Confidence is below the 0.90 level needed to auto-authorize a repair, so this is escalated for human approval of replace_servo_drive on CNC-02.

CNC-05 has a genuine hydraulic pressure leak (failing seals, a weakening pump, or a sticking relief valve). Its hydraulic pressure fell steadily from a 62.725 bar mean (ticks 1000–1059) to a 57.108 bar mean (ticks 1240–1290), reached 54.29 bar below the 55 bar alarm setpoint at tick 1281, and was still declining at tick 1300 (56.18 bar, −0.153 bar/tick) while CNC-05 is idle — the manual's leak pattern (pressure keeps falling while the station sits idle, unlike normal draw during a heavy cut, which would recover). CNC-02, the only other hydraulics-equipped machine, is running and stable (mean 68.78 bar, slightly rising over ticks 1290–1300), so this is CNC-05-specific, not a supply-wide problem. Passing inspections do not rule it out: some jobs still pass while clamping weakens. The exact leaking component (seal vs pump vs relief valve) is not distinguished, but all are addressed by the same seal-repair action.

CNC-02 has a localized hydraulic fault: pressure is leaking away (failing seals or a weakening pump), not a shared-supply problem. CNC-02's hydraulic_pressure fell stepwise across five consecutive 30-tick blocks (means 60.924 → 59.915 → 59.072 → 58.644 → 57.304), bottoming at 54.46 bar below the 55.00 bar setpoint that triggered the tick-1041 alarm. The only other hydraulic stations, CNC-05 and CNC-07, stayed flat at about 68–69 bar over the same window (CNC-07 mean 68.799 in the last block), ruling out a common supply, and CNC-02 is running with hydraulics fitted. The decline is smooth and progressive with no self-recovery, matching the manual's seal-leak pattern rather than an erratic transducer fault.
